# Pinned statement — run SEALED49 (this document is the entire problem context)

## Definitions

All graphs are finite simple graphs. For m a positive integer write
[m] = {0, 1, ..., m−1}; every named graph below has vertex set [m] for its
stated m.

**Alternating path.** For a ≥ 2, P_a^alt is the graph on [a] whose a−1 edges
are the consecutive pairs of the sequence (0, a−1, 1, a−2, 2, a−3, ...).
Examples: a = 4: sequence (0,3,1,2), edges {0,3},{3,1},{1,2}.
a = 5: sequence (0,4,1,3,2), edges {0,4},{4,1},{1,3},{3,2}.

**Dihedral group.** Dih(m) ≤ Sym([m]) is the subgroup generated by
ρ(i) = i+1 (mod m) and σ(i) = m−1−i.

**Γ-copy.** Let H be a graph on [m], Γ ≤ Sym([m]), and c a 2-coloring
(colors 1, 2) of the edges of the complete graph on vertex set [n]. For a
color r, a Γ-copy of H in color r consists of an increasing map
v : [m] → [n] (that is, v_0 < v_1 < ... < v_{m−1}) together with some γ ∈ Γ
such that for every edge {i, j} of H the pair {v_{γ(i)}, v_{γ(j)}} has
color r. Equivalently: some graph H′ in the orbit {γ(H) : γ ∈ Γ} — where
γ(H) has edge set {{γ(i), γ(j)} : {i,j} ∈ E(H)} — admits a monotone
color-r embedding i ↦ v_i.

**Dihedral Ramsey number.** For graphs H1 on [m1] and H2 on [m2],
R_dih(H1, H2) is the least n such that EVERY 2-coloring of the edges of the
complete graph on [n] contains a Dih(m1)-copy of H1 in color 1 or a
Dih(m2)-copy of H2 in color 2. Here K_b is the complete graph on [b]; note
that for K_b the Γ-copy notion coincides, for every Γ, with an ordinary
monochromatic b-clique.

**Sanity anchors (machine-checkable; verify before relying on them, derive
the general pattern yourself):** for 3 ≤ a ≤ 14 the orbit
{γ(P_a^alt) : γ ∈ Dih(a)} contains exactly a distinct graphs.

## The problem

Prove: for all integers a ≥ 4 and b ≥ 1,

    R_dih(P_a^alt, K_b) = 1 + (a − 1)(b − 1).

Both directions are in scope (the lower-bound construction and the upper
bound); the upper bound for general a ≥ 4 is the substantial content. Small
cases may be verified by any finite computation you can carry out yourself,
but per the completion bar, fixed-parameter verification does not constitute
resolution.
